items.title: Alignment by Confident Debate: Preference Learning from Multi-Agent Debate
items.abstract: This paper introduces Alignment by Confident Debate (AbCD), a method to learn preferences for language models without needing gold answers. AbCD uses a diverse committee of agents to debate problems, clustering their final answers by semantic equivalence to generate training data. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods by providing a principled way to derive supervision from self-generated debates, particularly for tasks lacking canonical answers.
items.figure_caption: Committee behavior for Qwen-2.5-1.5B-it on GSM8K. The committee size varies from one to five agents under independent sampling, after which the number of debate rounds is varied with five agents. Additional rounds increase agreement but do not improve consensus accuracy beyond the first exchange and can reduce correctness.

items.title: ROSE: Risk-Aware Orthogonal Subspace Navigation for Lifelong Knowledge Editing in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.abstract: ROSE tackles lifelong knowledge editing in MLLMs by restricting parameter updates to orthogonal subspaces, preventing interference with existing knowledge. It employs a risk-guided mechanism to protect crucial factual subspaces and uses multi-granularity integration during inference to precisely activate edited knowledge. This approach mitigates catastrophic forgetting and locality erosion, enabling stable and continuous model updates.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of optimization trajectories generated by conventional Editors and our ROSE. By navigating parameter updates away from high-risk general subspaces, ROSE achieves a superior balance between incorporating new knowledge and preserving pre-trained stability.

items.title: Assessing the Impact of Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Algorithmic Problem-Solving
items.abstract: This paper introduces a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) method to improve Large Language Models' performance on algorithmic problem-solving. The core method uses embedding-based retrieval and similarity search to find analogous problems from a knowledge base, with a dynamic threshold to reduce noise. Its contribution lies in demonstrating that this RAG approach, by providing relevant examples, significantly enhances LLMs' ability to solve competitive programming problems, particularly those similar to previously seen ones.

items.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
items.abstract: CPU-ARC introduces agentic reasoning caching to prevent LLMs from repeatedly solving the same problems. It converts LLM reasoning traces into efficient, CPU-executable caches (ARCs) that can reuse solutions for new problem instances. This method achieves comparable performance to LLMs on complex tasks while being significantly cheaper, explainable, and robust.

items.title: Knowing When to Intervene: Causal Evaluation of AI Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces a framework for evaluating the causal impact of interventions on AI agents during deployment. It addresses the limitation of static benchmarks by proposing a method to determine when and if interventions, like human review, are beneficial for an agent's final outcome. The core contribution is a causally grounded approach to assess the value of dynamic interventions in agentic AI systems.

items.title: Language as Trait, Politeness as Strategy: Controlled Tests of Linguistic Effects in LLM Social-Deduction Agents
items.abstract: This paper investigates how language complexity and politeness affect LLM agents' social deduction in the Werewolf game. By isolating and manipulating these linguistic features while preserving game content, the study found that neither language range nor politeness strategy significantly alters how other agents perceive or interact with a speaker. The core contribution is demonstrating that, within this controlled environment, these linguistic variations do not demonstrably impact trust, votes, or night actions.

items.title: LEMMO: A Large Electromagnetic Model leveraging Pretrained LLMs for Million-Sample Signal Understanding
items.abstract: LEMMO is a novel large electromagnetic model designed to understand long, raw signal recordings by leveraging pretrained LLMs. Its core method involves a linear-attention encoder and temporal resampling to process millions of samples, coupled with an EM-text interaction module that uses instruction-conditioned queries for recognition and detailed description. The paper's contribution lies in enabling instruction-driven analysis of extensive EM data, moving beyond traditional short-segment evaluations and facilitating comprehensive signal understanding.
items.figure_caption: Overview of LEMMO. Raw IQ signals are encoded and temporally compressed for long recordings. Instruction-conditioned queries retrieve signal evidence for a LoRA-adapted LLM, supporting recognition with 16 queries and detailed description with 128 structured queries.

items.title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
items.abstract: This paper introduces MemoryDojo, a benchmark designed to evaluate the vulnerability of LLM agent memory systems to poisoning attacks. The core method involves tracing how malicious information propagates through different memory architectures and measuring its impact on agent behavior across multi-session tasks. The key contribution is quantifying this susceptibility, revealing that all tested memory systems are vulnerable to poisoning, with significant variations in the severity of downstream effects.

items.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
items.abstract: This paper introduces Agentic Manipulation Policies (AMPs), where a generalist AI model directly controls a robot manipulator, adapting actions dynamically. The core contribution is demonstrating that these generalist AMPs outperform specialist policies like VLAs and WAMs, achieving state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on benchmarks and real-world tasks without task-specific training.
items.figure_caption: Zero-shot real-world manipulation with AMP1. AMP1 solves diverse, long-horizon manipulation tasks directly in the real world from a natural language instruction without task-specific fine-tuning or predefined skills. It devises complex strategies, such as ( A ) searching for hidden objects, ( B ) using a balance scale as a measuring instrument, ( C ) planning and executing a winning strategy in a game of chess, ( D ) combining non-prehensile and prehensile actions where a direct grasp is infeasible, and ( E ) manipulating articulated objects such as a kitchen cabinet door. Task instructions given to AMP1 for each episode are shown below the corresponding image sequence.

items.title: Test-Time Compute Scales Better with Parallel Agent Teams
items.abstract: This paper introduces "parallel agent teams" to improve test-time computation for fixed models. Instead of many independent agents or one large collaborative team, it samples many small teams in parallel and selects the best team's output. This approach achieves better performance than existing methods on long-horizon tasks, demonstrating improved scalability and efficiency.
items.figure_caption: Sample small teams, not agents or one big team. (a) Three ways to spend the same agents. A verifier keeps the best solution. (b) Qwen3.8-27B on four tasks. Parallel agents (blue) flatten quickly, one big team (green) rises and falls with its size, and parallel teams of ten (orange) keep improving. Brackets give the gain of parallel teams over each baseline at the largest budget both reach.

items.title: What to Delegate, What to Preserve: Human Preferences for Agentic AI Across Everyday Life and Work
items.abstract: This paper investigates human preferences for delegating tasks to AI agents across various life domains. Through a survey of 289 U.S. adults, the study found that trust, desired AI leadership, and anticipated financial benefits increase automation preference, while concerns about reduced personal fulfillment decrease it. The core contribution is identifying factors influencing delegation decisions and highlighting a preference for "bounded autonomy," where AI handles execution but humans retain oversight or involvement.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Overview of the survey procedure and scenario-sampling structure. Participants completed demographic and AI-background measures before evaluating one randomly selected task from each of nine domains, for a total of nine task evaluations per participant. Flow diagram of the survey procedure. Participants first completed demographic and AI-background questions, then evaluated nine task scenarios, with one task randomly selected from each of nine domains. Each participant therefore completed a total of nine task evaluations.

items.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
items.abstract: This paper proposes that embodied AI tasks can be solved by treating them as interactions with digital software. Their core method involves a "Computer-Use Agent" (CUA) that views a simulated physical environment through screenshots and controls it via keyboard/mouse actions, just like a human using software. The key contribution is demonstrating that a single CUA design, without task-specific tuning, can achieve high performance across diverse embodied tasks by leveraging general skills learned from software interaction.
items.figure_caption: Computer-use agents can operate any software through keyboard and mouse actions while observing the screen. We argue that physical environments are no different. Once exposed through software, they become just another interface for the same agent.

items.title: Know What You Need: Efficient Activation Checkpointing
items.abstract: This paper addresses the memory limitations in training large language models by improving Activation Checkpointing. Their core method is an **approximate rematerialization technique** that selectively recomputes important layer components during backpropagation, using information from the forward pass. This yields unbiased gradient estimates, significantly reducing the computational overhead of traditional checkpointing while achieving substantial memory savings.

items.title: One Run Is Not Enough: A Monte Carlo Protocol for Evaluating LLM Reliability on Data Science Tasks
items.abstract: This paper introduces DS-QA, a benchmark of 100 data science and statistics questions, to evaluate LLM reliability. It proposes a three-layer framework combining general, coarse-grained, and task-specific metrics. The core contribution is a Monte Carlo protocol with 100 repeated runs to assess response consistency and identify significant variability in LLM performance on complex data science tasks.
items.figure_caption: The proposed DS-QA contains three key components (cf. Sections 3 and 4 ). (1) A university-level data science benchmark, which covers 9 task types and 3 difficulty levels. (2) A multilayer evaluation framework, incorporating 4 general properties, 3 coarse-grained metrics, and in total 35 task-specific metrics. (3). A Monte Carlo analysis is used to study the reliability of LLM (text, code and image) outputs.

items.title: Compaction, decay and reinforcement in a two-tier conversational memory: a paired evaluation against retrieval-augmented generation
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel "compaction" method for conversational memory, where each turn is summarized into atomic facts, contrasting it with traditional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that keeps the full transcript. The core contribution is a rigorous paired evaluation demonstrating that compaction significantly outperforms RAG in generating accurate responses, especially when fewer prompt tokens are used, though its advantage diminishes on adversarial questions requiring verbatim recall.

items.title: Attend at the Right Resolution: Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention via Query-Key Interaction Structure
items.abstract: This paper proposes Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention (HASA), a training-free method to reduce the computational cost of attention in LLMs. HASA leverages the intrinsic interaction structure of pretrained attention heads to adaptively determine the optimal resolution for sparse attention selection, unlike previous methods that use fixed heuristics. This head-specific approach allows for more efficient and effective identification of relevant context tokens.
items.figure_caption: Motivation for HASA. Coarse-grained selection risks missing relevant tokens, while fine-grained selection increases selection overhead. HASA adapts selection granularity for each head.

items.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel radiology agentic framework that standardizes how an orchestrator calls modular AI tools to generate structured reports. The core contribution is demonstrating the potential of such a system, using FDA-cleared AI tools, to bridge the gap in radiology reporting by combining specialized and generalist AI capabilities. The framework aims to produce comprehensive reports across multiple modalities and body parts.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the framework. ( A ) Function catalog: 22 tool functions across 7 categories; functions are instantiated from the site-specific tool catalog. ( B ) Detailed signatures for two representative AI-vision functions, with required and optional parameters and the structured return type. ( C ) Orchestrator pipeline: clinical context (skills, RadReport.org template, patient data) is loaded by the Context Loader and feeds the Planner, which dispatches steps via the Grouper to parallel ReAct Loops that call tools from the available tool catalog; the Analyzer synthesises across tracks and may issue plan updates back to the Planner (feedback loop, dashed) before handing off to the Reporter and the Reviewer.

items.title: CID: Measuring Cognitive Work Through Semantic State Change
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Contextual Information Differential (CID), a novel metric to quantify "cognitive work" by measuring semantic state changes within a language model's embedding space. CID uses a covariance-aware Mahalanobis distance to track movement through this semantic space, offering a geometric approach to understanding and measuring meaning transformation. This provides a practical method for analyzing how information's meaning evolves.

items.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: This paper introduces Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL) to enhance long-term memory in model-based RL. Instead of architectural changes, it uses gradient descent at test time to encode episode-specific observations into the world model's parameters. This allows each episode to have a tailored world model, significantly improving memory capabilities for complex tasks.
items.figure_caption: Performance improvements brought by TT-MBRL on Memory Maze 2D and Memory Maze.

items.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
items.abstract: This paper proposes FlowAlign, a method for aligning multimodal data into a fixed target space. Its core method uses conditional flow matching during training to guide source representations towards the target space, ensuring both global structure and instance-level correspondence are preserved. The contribution lies in repurposing flow matching as a training signal to achieve a more robust and comprehensive alignment than existing methods.
items.figure_caption: Path-consistency score. (a) Field learning on paired source-to-target interpolation paths. (b) A compatible candidate representation yields a small velocity residual. (c) An incompatible candidate representation yields a large velocity residual.

items.title: Llama-modchip: 284B DeepSeek on 64GB RAM, no GPU
items.summary: This project demonstrates running the 284 billion parameter DeepSeek LLM on a 64GB RAM system without a GPU, showcasing efficient large model deployment.

items.title: I'm not convinced the AI bubble exists
items.summary: The author argues that current AI advancements are fundamentally different from past tech bubbles, suggesting a more sustainable and transformative future for the technology.

items.title: How I Fight AI Brain Fry
items.summary: This article offers practical strategies and personal experiences for managing the mental fatigue and overwhelm that can arise from extensive AI use.

items.title: Why I will not be using LLMs in my coding
items.summary: The author will not use LLMs for coding due to concerns about their potential to hinder learning, introduce subtle errors, and diminish the developer's own problem-solving skills.

items.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks
items.summary: Sherlock is a command-line tool that efficiently searches for social media profiles associated with a given username across numerous online platforms.

items.description: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE). A management plane for GPU Kubernetes on bare metal.
items.summary: NVKE is a management plane for GPU-accelerated Kubernetes clusters deployed on bare metal, enabling efficient orchestration of AI workloads.

items.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use
items.summary: OpenMausBot is an open-source Grok Bot alternative that provides a virtual machine for bots to operate within.

items.description: A collection of projects designed to help developers quickly get started with building deployable applications using the Claude API
items.summary: This repository provides ready-to-use projects that enable developers to rapidly build and deploy applications leveraging the Claude API.

items.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
items.summary: This repository provides a command-line interface for AI agents to automate browser interactions, enabling them to navigate websites, extract information, and perform actions programmatically.

items.description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready
items.summary: Meta's Astryx is an open-source, fully customizable design system designed for agent readiness, enabling flexible and adaptable user interface development.
This repository provides a collection of public "skills" that can be used to enhance the capabilities of AI agents, allowing them to perform a wider range of tasks and interact with external tools.

items.description: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.
items.summary: This repository provides MuJoCo, a general-purpose physics simulator for multi-joint dynamics with contact, enabling realistic simulations of complex mechanical systems.

items.description: A context-compression plugin for month-long single sessions (billions of tokens) ,small context windows (a 100K context is enough) and token savings (5x fewer tokens) .上下文压缩插件，月级长会话会话， 兼顾小窗口(100k上下文足矣)省token(省5倍token) . billion-context is all you need
items.summary: This GitHub repository provides a context-compression plugin that enables month-long single sessions with billions of tokens, achieving this with a small 100K context window and reducing token usage by 5x.

papers.title: LEMMO: A Large Electromagnetic Model leveraging Pretrained LLMs for Million-Sample Signal Understanding
papers.abstract: LEMMO is a novel large electromagnetic model designed to understand long, raw signal recordings by leveraging pretrained LLMs. Its core method involves a linear-attention encoder and temporal resampling to process millions of samples, coupled with an EM-text interaction module that uses instruction-conditioned queries for recognition and detailed description. The paper's contribution lies in enabling instruction-driven analysis of extensive EM data, moving beyond traditional short-segment evaluations and facilitating comprehensive signal understanding.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of LEMMO. Raw IQ signals are encoded and temporally compressed for long recordings. Instruction-conditioned queries retrieve signal evidence for a LoRA-adapted LLM, supporting recognition with 16 queries and detailed description with 128 structured queries.

papers.title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
papers.abstract: This paper introduces MemoryDojo, a benchmark designed to evaluate the vulnerability of LLM agent memory systems to poisoning attacks. The core method involves tracing how malicious information propagates through different memory architectures and measuring its impact on agent behavior across multi-session tasks. The key contribution is quantifying this susceptibility, revealing that all tested memory systems are vulnerable to poisoning, with significant variations in the severity of downstream effects.

papers.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Agentic Manipulation Policies (AMPs), where a generalist AI model directly controls a robot manipulator, adapting actions dynamically. The core contribution is demonstrating that these generalist AMPs outperform specialist policies like VLAs and WAMs, achieving state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on benchmarks and real-world tasks without task-specific training.
papers.figure_caption: Zero-shot real-world manipulation with AMP1. AMP1 solves diverse, long-horizon manipulation tasks directly in the real world from a natural language instruction without task-specific fine-tuning or predefined skills. It devises complex strategies, such as ( A ) searching for hidden objects, ( B ) using a balance scale as a measuring instrument, ( C ) planning and executing a winning strategy in a game of chess, ( D ) combining non-prehensile and prehensile actions where a direct grasp is infeasible, and ( E ) manipulating articulated objects such as a kitchen cabinet door. Task instructions given to AMP1 for each episode are shown below the corresponding image sequence.

papers.title: Test-Time Compute Scales Better with Parallel Agent Teams
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "parallel agent teams" to improve test-time computation for fixed models. Instead of many independent agents or one large collaborative team, it samples many small teams in parallel and selects the best team's output. This approach achieves better performance than existing methods on long-horizon tasks, demonstrating improved scalability and efficiency.
papers.figure_caption: Sample small teams, not agents or one big team. (a) Three ways to spend the same agents. A verifier keeps the best solution. (b) Qwen3.8-27B on four tasks. Parallel agents (blue) flatten quickly, one big team (green) rises and falls with its size, and parallel teams of ten (orange) keep improving. Brackets give the gain of parallel teams over each baseline at the largest budget both reach.

papers.title: What to Delegate, What to Preserve: Human Preferences for Agentic AI Across Everyday Life and Work
papers.abstract: This paper investigates human preferences for delegating tasks to AI agents across various life domains. Through a survey of 289 U.S. adults, the study found that trust, desired AI leadership, and anticipated financial benefits increase automation preference, while concerns about reduced personal fulfillment decrease it. The core contribution is identifying factors influencing delegation decisions and highlighting a preference for "bounded autonomy," where AI handles execution but humans retain oversight or involvement.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Overview of the survey procedure and scenario-sampling structure. Participants completed demographic and AI-background measures before evaluating one randomly selected task from each of nine domains, for a total of nine task evaluations per participant. Flow diagram of the survey procedure. Participants first completed demographic and AI-background questions, then evaluated nine task scenarios, with one task randomly selected from each of nine domains. Each participant therefore completed a total of nine task evaluations.

papers.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
papers.abstract: This paper proposes that embodied AI tasks can be solved by treating them as interactions with digital software. Their core method involves a "Computer-Use Agent" (CUA) that views a simulated physical environment through screenshots and controls it via keyboard/mouse actions, just like a human using software. The key contribution is demonstrating that a single CUA design, without task-specific tuning, can achieve high performance across diverse embodied tasks by leveraging general skills learned from software interaction.
papers.figure_caption: Computer-use agents can operate any software through keyboard and mouse actions while observing the screen. We argue that physical environments are no different. Once exposed through software, they become just another interface for the same agent.

papers.title: Know What You Need: Efficient Activation Checkpointing
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the memory limitations in training large language models by improving Activation Checkpointing. Their core method is an **approximate rematerialization technique** that selectively recomputes important layer components during backpropagation, using information from the forward pass. This yields unbiased gradient estimates, significantly reducing the computational overhead of traditional checkpointing while achieving substantial memory savings.

papers.title: One Run Is Not Enough: A Monte Carlo Protocol for Evaluating LLM Reliability on Data Science Tasks
papers.abstract: This paper introduces DS-QA, a benchmark of 100 data science and statistics questions, to evaluate LLM reliability. It proposes a three-layer framework combining general, coarse-grained, and task-specific metrics. The core contribution is a Monte Carlo protocol with 100 repeated runs to assess response consistency and identify significant variability in LLM performance on complex data science tasks.
papers.figure_caption: The proposed DS-QA contains three key components (cf. Sections 3 and 4 ). (1) A university-level data science benchmark, which covers 9 task types and 3 difficulty levels. (2) A multilayer evaluation framework, incorporating 4 general properties, 3 coarse-grained metrics, and in total 35 task-specific metrics. (3). A Monte Carlo analysis is used to study the reliability of LLM (text, code and image) outputs.

papers.title: Compaction, decay and reinforcement in a two-tier conversational memory: a paired evaluation against retrieval-augmented generation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel "compaction" method for conversational memory, where each turn is summarized into atomic facts, contrasting it with traditional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that keeps the full transcript. The core contribution is a rigorous paired evaluation demonstrating that compaction significantly outperforms RAG in generating accurate responses, especially when fewer prompt tokens are used, though its advantage diminishes on adversarial questions requiring verbatim recall.

papers.title: Attend at the Right Resolution: Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention via Query-Key Interaction Structure
papers.abstract: This paper proposes Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention (HASA), a training-free method to reduce the computational cost of attention in LLMs. HASA leverages the intrinsic interaction structure of pretrained attention heads to adaptively determine the optimal resolution for sparse attention selection, unlike previous methods that use fixed heuristics. This head-specific approach allows for more efficient and effective identification of relevant context tokens.
papers.figure_caption: Motivation for HASA. Coarse-grained selection risks missing relevant tokens, while fine-grained selection increases selection overhead. HASA adapts selection granularity for each head.

papers.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel radiology agentic framework that standardizes how an orchestrator calls modular AI tools to generate structured reports. The core contribution is demonstrating the potential of such a system, using FDA-cleared AI tools, to bridge the gap in radiology reporting by combining specialized and generalist AI capabilities. The framework aims to produce comprehensive reports across multiple modalities and body parts.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of the framework. ( A ) Function catalog: 22 tool functions across 7 categories; functions are instantiated from the site-specific tool catalog. ( B ) Detailed signatures for two representative AI-vision functions, with required and optional parameters and the structured return type. ( C ) Orchestrator pipeline: clinical context (skills, RadReport.org template, patient data) is loaded by the Context Loader and feeds the Planner, which dispatches steps via the Grouper to parallel ReAct Loops that call tools from the available tool catalog; the Analyzer synthesises across tracks and may issue plan updates back to the Planner (feedback loop, dashed) before handing off to the Reporter and the Reviewer.

papers.title: CID: Measuring Cognitive Work Through Semantic State Change
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Contextual Information Differential (CID), a novel metric to quantify "cognitive work" by measuring semantic state changes within a language model's embedding space. CID uses a covariance-aware Mahalanobis distance to track movement through this semantic space, offering a geometric approach to understanding and measuring meaning transformation. This provides a practical method for analyzing how information's meaning evolves.

papers.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL) to enhance long-term memory in model-based RL. Instead of architectural changes, it uses gradient descent at test time to encode episode-specific observations into the world model's parameters. This allows each episode to have a tailored world model, significantly improving memory capabilities for complex tasks.
papers.figure_caption: Performance improvements brought by TT-MBRL on Memory Maze 2D and Memory Maze.

papers.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
papers.abstract: This paper proposes FlowAlign, a method for aligning multimodal data into a fixed target space. Its core method uses conditional flow matching during training to guide source representations towards the target space, ensuring both global structure and instance-level correspondence are preserved. The contribution lies in repurposing flow matching as a training signal to achieve a more robust and comprehensive alignment than existing methods.
papers.figure_caption: Path-consistency score. (a) Field learning on paired source-to-target interpolation paths. (b) A compatible candidate representation yields a small velocity residual. (c) An incompatible candidate representation yields a large velocity residual.
